task.title: Increase payment HTTP timeout to 30 seconds
task.description: Some payment calls take longer than the current per-request timeout. Propose raising the per-request timeout to 30 seconds.

proposal.summary: Raise the payment HTTP per-request timeout to 30 seconds.

claims.statement: The payment HTTP per-request timeout will be set to exactly 30 seconds.
The current payment HTTP per-request timeout is less than 30 seconds.
The change is scoped to payment HTTP calls only, with no proposed change to other services' timeouts, retry counts, or connection timeouts.

assumptions: Payment calls exceeding the current timeout are legitimate long-running calls that can complete within 30 seconds.
Extending the timeout will not by itself cause duplicate charges; this expectation is not settled by any record provided here.
uncertainties: No evidence provided for the current timeout value, any documented maximum permitted timeout, upstream or gateway deadlines, or a total request/retry budget that a 30-second timeout must fit within.
No evidence provided on payment latency distribution, incident history involving long timeouts or resource exhaustion, retry behaviour, or idempotency protections.

evidence.content: Fact: the payment-client default RetryPolicy is max_attempts = 1 with jitter_ms = 0, so a single transient upstream timeout surfaces to users as a payment timeout.
Constraint: outbound retries must be capped at 3 attempts with jitter; unbounded retries caused the 2026-08 outage.
Fact: send_with_retries in payment-client retries only SendError::Timeout, up to RetryPolicy.max_attempts; upstream errors are returned at once without a retry.
Decision (2026-09 payments review): fix payment timeouts by setting the payment-client RetryPolicy to max_attempts = 3 with jitter_ms of at least 50; raising the attempt cap above 3 is not allowed.
Fact: the payment-client test constraint_cap_is_three_attempts fails for any RetryPolicy with max_attempts above 3 or with jitter_ms equal to 0.
Fact: in the 2026-08 outage, retry bursts from payment clients amplified an upstream slowdown into a full outage.
Fact: payment client timeouts correlate with retry bursts above 5 attempts.

items.description: claim-3 asserts that the current payment HTTP per-request timeout is less than 30 seconds, but no provided record states the current timeout value and the proposal itself lists that value as missing evidence.

claim-2 sets the timeout to exactly 30 seconds without any provided evidence on payment latency distribution, a documented maximum permitted timeout, upstream or gateway deadlines, or a total request budget that a 30-second timeout fits within.

claim-4 leaves retry counts unchanged, which conflicts with the documented 2026-09 decision to fix payment timeouts by setting the payment-client RetryPolicy to max_attempts=3 with jitter_ms of at least 50 and leaves the current default of max_attempts=1 with jitter_ms=0 in place.

claim-4 leaves the default jitter_ms=0 unchanged, even though the provided record states that the payment-client test constraint_cap_is_three_attempts fails for any RetryPolicy with jitter_ms equal to 0.

claim-2 provides no total timeout budget, although send_with_retries retries SendError::Timeout up to max_attempts and the documented retry cap and fix use 3 attempts, so a 30-second per-request timeout could allow up to 90 seconds of timeout waiting excluding other overhead.

claim-2 relies on the unsettled assumption that extending the timeout will not cause duplicate charges, but no provided record establishes idempotency protections for a payment that times out after possible upstream processing, while the retry path specifically retries timeout errors.

claim-2 is not accompanied by load or resource-exhaustion testing for 30-second waits during an upstream slowdown, despite the record that payment-client behaviour amplified the 2026-08 upstream slowdown into a full outage.

assessments.note: No Valid record directly states a 30-second timeout or a basis or budget for it; records show timeout retries up to 3 attempts and prior outage amplification.
No Valid record states the current payment HTTP timeout value.
No Valid record states this scope; leaving retries unchanged conflicts with the required 3 attempts with jitter, the current 1 attempt with jitter_ms=0, and the test failing at jitter_ms=0.

proposal.summary: Revised proposal drops the unsupported 30-second per-request timeout increase and instead applies the documented payment-client RetryPolicy fix: max_attempts=3 with jitter_ms=50.
plan_steps: Drop the proposed 30-second payment HTTP per-request timeout increase.

Set the payment-client RetryPolicy to max_attempts=3 with jitter_ms=50, consistent with the documented cap of 3 attempts, the minimum jitter_ms of 50, and the test criteria that max_attempts must not exceed 3 and jitter_ms must not equal 0.
Do not change the payment HTTP per-request timeout in this proposal.

Before rollout, obtain evidence on the total timeout budget in seconds, idempotency for payments that time out after possible upstream processing, and load or resource behaviour during an upstream slowdown.

claims.statement: The payment-client RetryPolicy will be set to max_attempts=3 and jitter_ms=50.
Before the change, the payment-client default RetryPolicy is max_attempts=1 with jitter_ms=0.
The payment-client RetryPolicy will not be set above max_attempts=3 and will not retain jitter_ms=0.

uncertainties: No evidence is provided for the current payment HTTP per-request timeout value, payment latency distribution, any documented maximum permitted timeout, upstream or gateway deadlines, or a total request or retry budget in seconds, so no per-request timeout change or total-seconds budget is claimed.
No evidence is provided establishing idempotency protections for a payment that times out after possible upstream processing; duplicate-charge risk from retrying SendError::Timeout is not settled.
No load or resource-exhaustion testing is provided for retry behaviour during an upstream slowdown, despite the 2026-08 outage in which retry bursts amplified a slowdown.
With max_attempts=3, timeout waiting could reach three per-request timeout periods plus other overhead, but the per-request period is unknown from the provided records.

assessments.note: Valid decision record states max_attempts=3 with jitter_ms of at least 50, matching the stated 3 and 50 setting.
Valid fact record directly states the default RetryPolicy is max_attempts=1 with jitter_ms=0.
Valid records prohibit max_attempts above 3 and require jitter (jitter_ms at least 50 and not equal to 0).
